newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram to address lawmakers on budget.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram to address lawmakers on budget.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to discuss the 1996/97 (April-March) budget in an address to the lower house of parliament on Tuesday afternoon, a ministry official said.
The finance minister is expected to make a general reply to points raised by parliamentary committees since he presented the budget blueprint to parliament on July 22, the official said.
Any specific concessions to industrial sectors would likely be made in a second address that Chidambaram plans to make next week, probably on September 9 or 10, the official said.

Chidambaram was expected to speak either just before the lower house, the Lok Sabha, adjourns for lunch, usually at about 1:30 p.m. (0800 GMT), or after it reconvenes at about 2:30 p.m. (0900 GMT), the official said.

Financial markets expect Chidambaram to offer concessions to selected industries, including relief from a proposed minimum corporate tax, and possibly announce measures to attract small investors to stock markets.
However, any such concessions were more likely to be announced in the remarks Chidambaram plans to make next week before the lower house, the official said.

Under the proposed budget, companies which currently do not pay income tax would have to pay a Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT), with an effective rate of 12 percent, on book profit. Companies in the power and infrastructure sectors would be exempted.
Some other sectors have been lobbying the government for at least a partial exemption from MAT.
Parliament is expected to vote on the budget plan by September 13, when the current session is scheduled to adjourn.
